articles.title: Días no laborables por la visita del Papa León XIV: ¿Cuántos son y hasta cuándo?
articles.summary: Visita del papa León XIV en Perú: ¿qué días serán no laborables en Lima, Callao, Chiclayo, Cusco y Pucallpa? El Gobierno peruano estableció días no laborables compensables en distintas regiones del país para facilitar el desplazamiento de la población y su participación en las actividades programadas por la visita del papa León XIV. Todos los detalles, en esta nota.
articles.body_text: Luego de que el Vaticano informara sobre la recuperación favorable del papa León XIV tras una intervención quirúrgica por un adenocarcinoma pulmonar, muchas instituciones y organizaciones continúan con la preparación para su visita al Perú. De hecho, el Gobierno nacional estima que la visita del Santo Padre al país podría movilizar a unas 854 000 personas, entre ellas más de 50 000 turistas extranjeros, quienes buscarán acercarse a él para recibir su bendición. Por ello, el Ejecutivo busca facilitar la participación de la población en las actividades que desarrollará el pontífice en las regiones que visitará, por lo que estableció días no laborables. Esta medida permitirá que los ciudadanos puedan asistir a los encuentros programados con Robert Prevost; sin embargo, las horas dejadas de trabajar deberán ser recuperadas posteriormente. En la siguiente nota te contamos todo lo que debes saber al respecto. A través del Decreto Supremo n.º 020-2026-TR, el Gobierno estableció días no laborables entre el 11 al 16 de noviembre para Lima, Callao, Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque, Piura, Cusco y Ucayali, con motivo a la visita del papa León XIV. Esta medida es compensable y se rige por normas distintas a las de los feriados. Es decir, en el sector público, las horas no laboradas deben recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores o en el plazo que establezca cada entidad. En tanto, en el sector privado, empleadores y trabajadores pueden acordar la forma de compensar esas horas. Si no llegan a un consenso, el empleador determina las condiciones para su recuperación. Por consiguiente, te presentamos, compartido por Infobae, los departamentos en las que regirá estos días de descanso: 11 de noviembre: 12 de noviembre: 13 de noviembre: 14 de noviembre: 15 de noviembre: 16 de noviembre: Durante su visita al Perú, el papa León XIV participará en una vigilia de oración junto a miles de jóvenes de entre 16 y 35 años, que se realizará el jueves 12 de noviembre, a las 6:00 p. m., en el Estadio Nacional. Asimismo, el lunes 16 presidirá la Santa Misa de clausura, programada para las 10:30 a. m. en la Base Aérea Las Palmas. Según los organizadores, los asistentes deberán contar con una entrada gratuita, que podrán obtener a través de las plataformas Teleticket y Ticketmaster. Sin embargo, quienes no puedan asistir a alguna de estas actividades por diversos motivos no podrán ceder su entrada a un familiar o ser querido, ya que los boletos son intransferibles y están vinculados a los datos personales registrados previamente por cada asistente, según informó el Arzobispado de Lima. Inclusive, indicaron que será indispensable presentar el documento de identidad en la puerta del recinto el día del evento, garantizando que el acceso sea gratuito.

articles.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Apple's new app for a study will answer everyday medical questions
articles.body_text: Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people. The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months. The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys. Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results to get more personalized and pointed suggestions from the app. The company said the app can also help prepare participants better for a doctor’s visit, and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues. Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours. “At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in a statement, adding, “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.” The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users. It’s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet. The potential is huge — earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week . articles.title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Bharat Semi says it has secured design wins for its AI-enabled sensor technology with companies including General Atomics.
articles.body_text: Bharat Semi , an Indian semiconductor startup, has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors, as it seeks to win customers in the United States and elsewhere. The investment comes as the nearly five-year-old, pre-revenue startup says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense technology company General Atomics and India’s Kaynes Semicon. Its image sensors, however, remain under development, with the startup targeting its initial commercial production in 2027. India has committed billions of dollars to build up a domestic semiconductor industry, with a hope to become an alternative manufacturing hub as U.S. companies look to diversify supply chains beyond China. The country, however, has yet to establish itself as a major chip manufacturing hub. Meanwhile, the AI boom is also giving Indian startups such as Bharat Semi an opportunity to develop specialized chips for global markets. The New Delhi-based startup is developing programmable image sensors that combine image capture, processing, and AI capabilities on a single chip, reducing the need to send visual data to separate processors. The move could cut system costs by at least 70% compared with conventional setups that use a separate image sensor, image signal processor, and a system-on-chip, co-founder Vrinda Kapoor (pictured above, right) said in an interview. “Our aim here is to move from sensors to sense-making solutions,” Kapoor told TechCrunch. Kapoor, a South Park Commons fellow who earlier worked in healthcare technology, co-founded Bharat Semi in late 2021 with Vinayak Dalmia (pictured above, left), the startup’s managing director, who previously worked at McKinsey and in private equity. Its chief technology officer, Boyd Fowler, previously held the same role at image-sensor maker OmniVision. Bharat Semi is targeting smart homes, industrial automation, surveillance, and aerospace. Without disclosing specifics, Kapoor pointed to air conditioners that could detect when a room is empty and adjust automatically and drones that could process visual information — even with the absence of more expensive computing hardware elsewhere in the system. The startup’s first-generation sensors are already in prototyping, while its second-generation sensors, which will incorporate more advanced AI capabilities, are expected to reach the prototype stage by mid-2027, Kapoor said. Moreover, the startup plans to get those newer sensors into customers’ hands by the end of 2027. The all-equity seed round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indus Bridge Ventures, with participation from Valour Capital, Micromax, Gaingels, and individual investors. Bharat Semi, Kapoor said, plans to use the funding to expand its engineering team, complete product development, and bring its sensors to market. Bharat Semi has about 75 employees across India and the U.S., including 10 to 12 in its American operations, which span engineering and business development in Santa Clara. The startup plans to increase its U.S. headcount to around 20 by mid-2027, Kapoor said. It has also begun hiring engineers in Europe. “It’s a story of can we build a global technology company out of India,” Kapoor said. In 2024, Bharat Semi announced plans for a semiconductor fabrication project in India involving a technology partnership with the U.S. Space Force. The initiative, Kapoor said, remains in development and the startup is working to identify domestic partners that would build and operate the facility.

articles.title: Is bad news for Jensen Huang also bad news for the AI industry? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: "Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia."
articles.body_text: We didn’t see this coming. Or at least, I didn’t — a week ago, when I wrote about Nvidia’s board opening an investigation into then-CEO Jensen Huang, I assumed his job was safe. On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Rebecca Bellan, Tim De Chant, and I discussed how Huang’s ouster went down and what it means for the larger AI economy. While Tim said he saw it coming (albeit not this quickly), Rebecca said, “I didn’t think it was going to happen at all.” “Jensen is Nvidia, right?” she added. “And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia.” Similarly, I marveled at how quickly Huang’s support seemed to crumble, with more scandals seeming to emerge every day. (At the same time, there are many who’d still like to see him return .) And we also took a moment to wonder what will happen to Nvidia’s investments in the larger AI ecosystem. Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity; you can listen to the whole episode here . Tim De Chant: I figured this was coming. I didn’t think it would happen this quickly. I thought there would be at least a few days. Rebecca Bellan: I didn’t think it was going to happen at all. I mean, Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia. And we’ve got nothing but the last few years of data to show us that billionaires can do whatever the hell they want. So it was surprising to me — it almost restored my faith in humanity, that he resigned. But someone said to me, “If this were Elon, nothing would happen.” He would not be resigning. Nothing would be going down Anthony Ha: Which is interesting, because I would have said, as of a week ago, or even just a few days ago, that Jensen is in the same category as Elon. I mean, no one is quite as special as Elon is, but it’s a big, incredibly successful company. Like you said — in a lot of ways, the entire AI economy is built on top of Nvidia. And for most people, Jensen Huang is Nvidia. He’s the biggest shareholder. He has family members who work at the company, and probably most importantly, there was no succession plan in place. So this was not something that they were prepared for at all. Rebecca: I think we should actually take a step back, because we just launched into this conversation assuming — rightly so — that our listeners will know what the heck we’re talking about. But for those who somehow don’t, Jensen resigned on Thursday, after it came out he was having an affair with a former executive at an Nvidia customer called Megaspeed, who’s alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence. And then there was another reported affair with an Nvidia executive.

articles.title: SNL gathers all the tech tycoons for a lesson in dating and spycraft | TechCrunch
articles.summary: While awkward, creepy tech executives have become a recurring theme on Saturday Night Live, this week’s episode gave the cast a chance to show off all their impressions at once.
articles.body_text: While awkward, creepy tech executives have become a recurring theme on Saturday Night Live, this week’s episode gave the cast a chance to show off all their impressions at once. In a single sketch, we got James Austin Johnson as Peter Thiel, Ben Marshall as Sam Altman, Jane Wickline as Dario Amodei, Jeremy Culhane as Elon Musk, Andrew Dismukes as Mark Zuckerberg — and eventually, the recently departed Bowen Yang joined the fun as Jensen Huang. Huang’s ouster from Nvidia (after admitting to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy) could have serious implications for the tech industry ; it also provided a hook for some obvious jokes about rich nerds being easy marks for women (or men) who are out of their league. In the sketch, a CIA agent played by host John Mulaney (hilarious as ever, if not entirely confident about how to pronounce “Palantir” or “Nvidia”) attempts to painstakingly explain why these execs should be suspicious when someone attractive suddenly seems interested in them romantically. For Altman and Thiel’s sake, he added, “I hope this is obvious: Even though you’re gay, you can still be tricked by a spy.” Johnson’s version of Thiel pushed back, insisting that tech tycoons deserve more respect, given all they’ve done for the country. “Name one time technology has let us down,” he said, giving Mulaney a chance to remind viewers about flights being halted all across the United States on Friday night. “Okay, name one more time,” the fictional Thiel said, leading to an obligatory mention of Microsoft Outlook going down on Thursday . When asked for a third example, Mulaney said, “No, I’m done naming times.” “Look, I get it,” he said. “I can’t imagine how disorienting this has been for you, to go from being bug-eyed weirdos to being gods. I mean, never in the history of our species have people as pale and as strange as you a) survived, and b) been given all the world’s wealth and power.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Flaming Hydra’s new Kickstarter campaign rethinks e-book ownership and digital lending | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A new Kickstarter campaign aims to usher in the “return of the human internet.”
articles.body_text: Here’s a big promise: A new Kickstarter campaign aims to usher in the “return of the human internet.” That’s the tagline of a crowdfunding campaign for The Phoenix Project , an initiative from the online culture and commentary magazine Flaming Hydra . If you back The Phoenix Project, you’re supporting three things — a one-off print magazine designed to celebrate “the values and fun of the early internet,” a new e-book service for libraries, and a newsletter subscription/archiving program that’s also designed for libraries. To Flaming Hydra’s lead editor Maria Bustillos, these disparate projects are “basically all one thing,” tied together by the goal of “protecting freedom of information” and fulfilling the “promise of the early internet, where you’re making information available to as many people as possible, while still protecting the right of artists and authors to make a living.” Bustillos told me that these issues have been highlighted on Flaming Hydra itself, for example when Tal Levin wrote about finding countless AI-generated clones of his book on Amazon. By “creating an ecosystem that is based in people working together, who are offering their stuff in a context that is controlled and doesn’t allow” others to create and sell AI-generated clones, Bustillos said Flaming Hydra is “part of the human project.” “AI is not this unstoppable force,” she added. “If people just set up publishing pipelines and networks and organizations that are dedicated to the human internet, people who want to read stuff can go to them, and it’s actually completely isolated from mechanistic interference.” The Phoenix Project fits into this vision by making the work of human writers more accessible to libraries. Back in 2020, Bustillos wrote about the e-book systems dominating libraries and schools. In one example, instead of just buying a book, a school had to pay $27 per student per year for continued access to copies of “The Diary of Anne Frank.” This is symptomatic of a broader system that treats true ownership of e-books and other digital media as a thing of the past. Instead, we “license” these e-books from their publishers, and they can be altered or removed at any time. “E-books are books,” Bustillos said. “They’re not some other thing. They are books, and people should be able to own them, and libraries should be able to own them, and media should be able to be owned. All digital media should be able to be owned.” In her view, ownership boils down to a simple question: “If you are at the mercy of somebody who can shut the book off, you do not own it.” So even beyond the question of ongoing payments, there have also been examples of e-books being altered or removed from readers’ devices long after their purchase. Bustillos acknowledged that for individual pieces of media, this distinction may not seem like a big deal, “but if it’s all the textbooks for everybody, if it’s all the books,” then it’s a real problem. Flaming Hydra and The Phoenix Project seek to solve this by letting libraries truly purchase and own e-books. They can then lend those e-books to their patrons through a new, open source “library in a box” system called Lenny for Libraries .

articles.title: The tech products we enthusiastically recommend this holiday season | TechCrunch
articles.summary: We've been reviewing a bunch of new gadgets at TechCrunch this year, and we have some clear favorites to share for your Black Friday shopping and beyond.
articles.body_text: We’ve been reviewing a bunch of new gadgets and hardware at TechCrunch this year: dumb phones , bird feeders , health trackers , slushy machines , AI mattress pads , you name it. Sometimes we think they’re unnecessary and expensive , but other times, we try out devices that we love so much that we go out and buy them ourselves. If these products can impress a group of (sometimes) curmudgeonly tech reporters, then they’re sure to please whoever you’re shopping for this holiday season. We’ve reviewed a lot of e-readers this year. What can we say? We’re nerds. We work for a tech website. But after trying devices from the usual suspects as well as some wildcards, we have recommendations. Evidently, 2026 was the year we fell in love with the pocket-sized e-reader. It’s an e-reader so small that it can fit in your wallet, or even magnetize to the back of your phone. Do you dream of a world where instead of scrolling Instagram when you’re waiting in line for coffee, you actually opt to read books? There’s really something special about the X3, and it’s only $55 during Xteink’s Black Friday sale. Fair warning, it takes some fiddling with to set up, and it has no integration with Kindle, Libby, or any other apps, so only buy this for someone willing to do a bit of Reddit browsing and tinkering to get it up and running. If you aren’t planning to magnetize the XTeink to your phone, you’ve got to go with the X4 Pro . It’s slightly bigger, but it has a backlight, which makes it way more versatile. After using both the X3 and the X4 Pro, I find that the backlight really is a game changer, since I do a lot of reading in bed — plus, I like my Pop Socket wallet a bit too much to displace for the X3, and I’d rather just carry an extra credit card-sized device than risk forgetting my actual credit and ID cards, which I have grown too used to having on my phone. If I’m being honest, reading my colleague Aisha Malik’s review of the Boox Palma Pro 2 is making me want to buy one. I love using the Xteink e-readers, but they don’t connect to any outside apps. As a hardcore Libby power user (a phrase I am saying in earnest sincerity), it’s a bit frustrating that I can’t get my library books on Xteink e-readers. The same goes for apps like Kobo and Kindle, where any e-book you already own cannot be transferred out of the Amazon ecosystem unless the publisher agrees, which most do not. If you’re looking for an e-reader with a screen that’s actually book-sized, my favorite that I’ve used is the Kobo Libra Colour , which is $259. The Amazon Paperwhite line is great, but c’mon, Amazon. Branch out! Hey, we’ve all got to eat. And if you want, you can make that eating process overly techy. Why not? The Ember Mug 3 is the latest iteration in Ember’s line of coffee/tea cups that actually stay warm. Our reviewer Lauren Forristal especially appreciated that you no longer need to use your phone app to change the mug’s temperature, which seems like it would be really annoying! This mug is perfect for gifting to someone, or to put on your own wishlist — you might not want to spend $99 on a mug for yourself, but these sorts of luxury, nice-to-haves are what holidays are made for! Ah, Ninja, the premiere company in the business of turning every appliance into a two-in-one air fryer. I jest, but at least Ninja knows it’s onto something. Despite the high price point, Lauren says that this new product made “a pretty convincing case for ditching two appliances and making room for one.” You can’t buy more counter space (without moving), but you can buy more versatile appliances. Sure, there are cheaper ice makers on the market. But Aisha clarifies that this is the ice maker for “those who crave what’s called ‘the good ice.’” If you feel so passionately about the ice in your beverages that you know what she means, then maybe this is for you.

articles.title: Where was Nvidia's security team? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia’s security chief quietly left in August, and now that CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down over his relationships, including one with an executive at a company suspected of funneling chips to China, a former intelligence officer says it’s the kind of leak that runs everyday conversations, which most corporate security teams are poorly equipped to catch.
articles.body_text: Outsiders had little reason to notice when Nvidia’s longtime chief security officer and head of product security stepped down in August. Just two and a half months later, CEO Jensen Huang himself left the company over growing questions about his extramarital relationships — starting with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore data center company that U.S. investigators suspect of funneling Nvidia chips to China, then widening to reports about two separate affairs with Nvidia employees. At the time, David Reber, who spent four years as CSO and seven at Nvidia overall, said he was leaving for health reasons. “This wasn’t a pivot I had planned. But I know what needs to come first: family and health,” he wrote on LinkedIn in late August, disclosing that he’d been diagnosed with young-onset Parkinson’s more than two years ago. Reber’s replacement, Saša Zdjelar, previously spent 17 years at ExxonMobil in Houston, leaving as a senior IT manager before spending one year at Salesforce and several years at the cybersecurity company ReversingLabs. Zdjelar didn’t respond to questions Thursday about the transition or what the security team knew. Nothing public connects Reber’s or Zdjelar’s role changes to the Megaspeed matter, but it seems fair to wonder what Nvidia’s security team knew about the government’s scrutiny of Megaspeed and about Huang’s relationships, and whether anyone raised concerns. Reber didn’t respond to questions Thursday. Nvidia also has not answered our related questions. Relationships between a CEO and his employees typically fall to HR, legal and the board, not security. But security specialists say any affair — even one inside the office — can give a foreign intelligence service leverage over an exec who wants it kept quiet. Still, spotting the clues isn’t easy. The way intelligence services collect information, much of it through everyday conversation rather than hacking, makes it especially difficult for security teams to identify risks, according to retired senior intelligence officer Nicholas Eftimiades, who says he has trained more than 1,000 corporate security professionals. Some people inside Nvidia clearly knew parts of the picture. Nvidia’s top lawyer was engaged with the government’s Megaspeed inquiry more than a year ago, The New York Times reported earlier this week . (Nvidia has said it regularly contacts officials.) Reports about Huang’s relationships with employees suggest colleagues also knew of them, even if the behavior is not expressly forbidden by Nvidia’s code of conduct . The Times cited five Nvidia employees who said he was involved with a vice president who reported directly to him; Reuters, citing two people, later reported a second relationship. What’s unclear is whether any of that reached security. Even if it had, Eftimiades, who wrote Chinese Espionage Operations and Tactics in 2020, told TechCrunch that a security team’s resources are often limited. For one thing, they’re often underfunded because, unlike some other cost centers, they don’t drive revenue. It’s astonishingly common for CEOs to answer a security team’s warnings with “not a nickel more than compliance,” he said. Many companies also define security overly narrowly, specialists say. In an opinion piece in The Hill , Don Aviv, CEO of the corporate investigations firm Interfor International, and author Jeremy Hurewitz, wrote, “Too many companies still approach security primarily as a matter of protecting facilities, preventing cyberattacks, and responding to physical threats.” The two argued that “[s]ecurity teams need to pay greater attention to insider threats, including the cultivation of executives and employees by foreign intelligence services, suspicious business relationships, conflicts of interest and attempts to obtain sensitive information through trusted personal contacts.” It would be surprising if Nvidia’s security team didn’t have a more expansive remit than most companies given its scale and business partners, but it’s possible. In fairness, some of it is simply beyond what any team can do. Speaking generally, not about Huang, Eftimiades offered a hypothetical in which a CEO complains that he can’t do something because “I’m fighting a board who doesn’t want to do this.” That tells an intelligence asset who the obstacle is. The service then asks, “Who’s the sticking point here?” and looks for ways into that person’s email and phone. What a rival intelligence service wants is often less technology than policy insight, including who’s pushing to change export rules and who the biggest blocker is. “Intel world tends to be like cancer,” he said. “Once it gets into the body, it looks to spread and looks to reach out.”

articles.title: Tesla opens Cybercab pre-orders ‘for personal use,’ with geo restrictions and a $299 monthly fee | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Even Elon Musk said the monthly fee is "too high."
articles.body_text: Tesla said on Friday evening that “select customers” now have the opportunity to pre-order the company’s autonomous, golden Cybercab “for personal use.” More details became clear as those select customers looked at the order page. Tech reviewer Marques Brownlee posted that buyers “must accept delivery” in one of a handful of Texas cities and that the Cybercab will only operate in certain geofenced areas. The estimated delivery date is December 2026. In addition to the $29,990 price tag, Cybercab owners will need to pay $299 per month to operate their vehicle. In response to Brownlee’s post, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the Cybercab “will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval.” He added that the monthly fee is “too high”: “Should match the cost of Tesla [Full Self-Driving] and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.” Tesla’s Ashok Elluswamy offered more information about the geofencing, saying that Cybercab will work “unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as @robotaxi, just serving the owners’ needs.” After falling far short of projected sales, Tesla recently announced it will cease Cybertruck production next year and use the additional factory capacity to build more Cybercabs. articles.body_text: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Saturday that a nationwide ground stop halting flights across the United States was caused by seemingly routine maintenance work. Duffy said that during “routine maintenance,” copper wire at a remote location was upgraded to fiber optic cable by L3Harris, a longtime contractor for the Federal Aviation Administration. After the upgrade, a router overloaded a critical communication system, leading to the ground stop. “It’s pretty straightforward work that we were doing yesterday at, again, a very remote location,” Duffy said during a Saturday press conference that appeared to have technical issues of its own . “What we’re working to determine was whether we had incompetence — meaning, was it user error or [installer] error from L3Harris? Or did they install a faulty router?” The FAA’s acting CTO Rebecca Guy added , “When we started to see the occurrence where our network was having instability, we started to look at what was the cause. And as such, we saw two places that were actually pinging our network at a very high rate — a thousand connections over every four to five seconds.” Guy said the FAA disabled “both of those, right away and were able to stabilize our network,” and is now performing a root cause analysis. Duffy has repeatedly insisted, at multiple press conferences, that Congress needs to provide more funding for aviation equipment upgrades. Asked why the upgrades were made at 3pm on a Friday afternoon — rather than, say, at midnight on a Saturday — he responded that while “switchovers” at bigger airports will take place late at night, remote switchovers happen during the day. “There will be reevaluation of when we do this work,” he said. This was only the third nationwide ground stop of the 21st century. More than 8,200 flights were canceled on Friday evening, according to aviation data firm Cirium . And the effects continued after the ground stop was lifted, with at least another 3,000 flights canceled on Saturday. The ground stop came just a day after the FAA announced the rollout of an AI tool for air traffic controllers; the air traffic controllers union said it was not consulted in designing the system. However, FAA administrator Bryan Bedford said the agency sees “zero evidence of anything nefarious and zero evidence of anything AI-related.” “We want to be clear that we have an equipment issue, and we’re working through what this defective piece of equipment was,” Bedford said. When Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin was asked earlier if the ground stop was caused by AI, he replied , “We call it SI [ super intelligence ] around here, remember? articles.body_text: Världsledare ”blickar bortom Trump”, skriver Politico . Man ”ser honom som försvagad” av resultatet i mellanårsvalet. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. President Donald Trump ”kommer att möta en okänd dynamik” när han flyger till Asien den här veckan för två toppmöten, enligt Politico. – Asiatiska ledare kommer att se presidenten som något försvagad nu, säger Kurt Tong som tidigare haft en vice ministerpost vid amerikanska utrikesdepartementet. Ledarna ”är inte lika rädda för Trumps vrede” efter att hans parti nyligen förlorade kontrollen över kongressen i mellanårsvalet, uppger källor för Politico. Trumps Asienresa kan ge de första antydningarna om i vilken grad utländska ledare ”ser honom hasa mot en sorti snarare än att dominera världsscenen”. Ledarna ”kommer att hantera Trump försiktigt men hålla sina alternativ öppna”, enligt en asiatisk diplomat. – Även om de fortfarande ser en relation med USA som viktig betyder det inte nödvändigtvis att de kommer att göra som Trump vill, säger diplomaten. En annan asiatisk diplomat sade att deras land är mindre intresserat av att ingå nya avtal med Trump och hellre väntar in en ny administration efter presidentvalet 2028. – Det kommer att finnas mindre entusiasm för att göra affärer med Trump-administrationen, säger diplomaten. Trump kommer att träffa den kinesiske presidenten Xi Jinping under resan. – Kineserna funderar redan mer på vad som kommer härnäst än på hur de ska hantera Trump, säger Jonathan Czin, ex-CIA-analytiker om Kina.

articles.title: Bakslaget för Putin: Tar inget
articles.summary: Ryssland har inte gjort några framsteg på slagfältet i Ukraina i år. Den slutsatsen drar tankesmedjan ISW i en ny analys.
articles.body_text: Ryssland har inte gjort några framsteg på slagfältet i Ukraina i år. Den slutsatsen drar tankesmedjan ISW i en ny analys. Det beskrivs som ”Putins stora huvudvärk” av danska B.T. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Rysslands president Vladimir Putin ”står inför en obekväm sanning” om landets brist på framsteg på slagfältet i Ukraina under året. Det skriver B.T. om tankesmedjan ISW:s nya analys. ”De ryska styrkorna har praktiskt tagit inte gjort några nettoframsteg under 2026. Samtidigt har det kostat dem över 40 000 soldater i månaden sedan juli”, skriver ISW. – Om vi ​​bortser från all storpolitik är det min bedömning att tiden arbetar för ukrainarna eftersom de ryska förlusterna är så höga, säger Rysslandsexperten Flemming Splidsboel till B.T. USA:s specialsändebud Jared Kushner skrev tidigare under månaden att ett fredsavtal kring kriget i Ukraina måste inkludera ”den bredare europeiska säkerhetsarkitekturen”. Rysslands president Vladimir Putin har riktat flera krav för att det ska kunna bli fred i Ukraina, bland annat att Finland ska lämna Nato. Ryssland försöker låtsas att det går bra på slagfältet för att stå starkare i fredsförhandlingarna, enligt Splidsboel. – I princip kan Vladimir Putin inte fortsätta skicka soldater till fronten för alltid, men vi vet helt enkelt inte när Ryssland kommer att nå den punkten. Han har gjort det till en kamp för Rysslands existens. Om Ryssland förlorar så är det slut med Ryssland som stat, säger Splidsboel. Tidigare i veckan läckte uppgifter om att 450 000 ryssar hade mist livet i kriget efter att hackare slagit till mot ryska statistikbyrån Rosstat. – Ryssarna är villiga att offra unga män på ett sätt vi inte förstår. Och det är också det som förklarar varför Ryssland kan fortsätta att kasta in så många soldater i kriget, säger Splidsboel.

articles.title: Kungen: Detta är min största ånger
articles.summary: Kung Charles har pratat om sin största ånger som gjorde honom ”besviken”, enligt en vän.
articles.body_text: Kung Charles har pratat om sin största ånger som gjorde honom ”besviken”, enligt en vän. – Han ville alltid åka dit, säger vännen till The Sunday Times . Nu har kungen fått ett erbjudande om att få sin dröm uppfylld. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Kung Charles skilde sig från sin fru prinsessan Diana 1996 och hon dog i en bilolycka året därpå. Han hade under flera år knappt någon kontakt med sonen prins Harry och fick då inte träffa sin två små barnbarn. Men en av sakerna kungen ångrar mest i livet är något helt annat, enligt en vän. Butlin’s är en brittisk kedja med semesteranläggningar som erbjuder lek, bad och andra familjeaktiviteter. Den grundades med tanken att erbjuda prisvärda semestrar för vanliga familjer. Charles ska enligt vännen alltid ha ångrat att han aldrig hade en Butlin’s-semester. – När man får kungen att prata om saker han ångrar att han inte gjort är en av dem att han aldrig har varit på Butlin’s, att han och prinsessan Anne aldrig var där som barn, säger kungens vän till The Sunday Times. Men föräldrarna drottning Elizabeth och prins Philip satte stopp för Charles barndomsdröm. – Han frågade drottningen och prins Philip många gånger om han och Anne kunde åka på semester till Butlin’s som barn och han berättar hur drottningen alltid svarade: ”Jag tror inte riktigt att vi kommer att kunna göra det.” Han skrattar åt hur besviken han var över att han och hans syster aldrig lyckades med det som barn. Han ville alltid åka dit, säger vännen. Det finns för närvarande tre brittiska Butlin’s-anläggningar som ligger vid Minehead, Bognor Regis och Skegness. Efter kungens 78-årsdag i helgen och uppgifterna i Sunday Times-artikeln sade en talesperson för Butlin’s: – Vi vill önska hans majestät ett stort grattis på födelsedagen och hjälpa honom att förverkliga en barndomsönskan. Hans avlidna mor besökte Butlin’s 1963 och vi bjuder gärna in kungen och hans familj att besöka en av våra anläggningar.

Konservativa profiler såsom Matt Walsh, Ben Shapiro och Steve Bannon har alla varit kritiska efter valförlusten. Walsh är den som har gått hårdast åt Trump och sagt att ”kapitlet Trump är avslutat”. – Trump är en extremt impopulär, 80-årig president på väg ut, utan trovärdighet hos väljarna, utan framtid och nu också utan någon verklig makt, sa han, rapporterar New York Times. De två podcastavsnitten som han har publicerat sedan valet har handlat om dinosaurier och om människans utveckling. På onsdagen närmade han sig politiken igen. – Allt är vidrigt. articles.body_text: C väljer den rödgröna sidan – men kravet på att V ska stå utanför regeringen ligger fast. Nu ökar pressen på S och V rejält, menar statsvetaren Jenny Madestam. – Brottningsmatchen mellan Andersson och Dadgostar, där måste det ske någon slags ”slutstrid”. De måste hitta en lösning. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Efter att ha granskat ”totalpaketen” från statsministerkandidaterna har Centerpartiet nu gjort ett val i regeringsfrågan. C-ledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist meddelade på söndagskvällen att partiet vill ingå i en rödgrön regering med Socialdemokraterna och Miljöpartiet, men kräver fortsatt att Vänsterpartiet ska stå utanför. – Syftet för C med att ta in de här två ”offerterna” har varit att visa att om V inte backar kan vi tänka oss att gå över till det andra alternativet om det är riktigt saftigt. Men jag tror att det här har varit viktigt för C också, att det har blivit lättare för partiet att komma vidare i processen när man har fått ta ställning till de sakpolitiska förslagen, säger Jenny Madestam, statsvetare vid Södertörns högskola. Hon tror inte att matematiken – att en borgerlig fyrpartiregering skulle behöva SD:s stöd för att få igenom sin politik – spelat så stor roll för C i vägvalet. Däremot har C sannolikt tagit hänsyn till att partiets väljare räknat med att få en rödgrön regering och den svåra svekdebatt som skulle komma om man hade vänt sig högerut i stället, tror Madestam. Under de senaste dagarna har företrädare för S, V och MP varnat för att en högerregering skulle vara helt beroende av SD och kallat ett sidbyte för ett ”historiskt svek”. – C vet var man har sina väljare. Jag tror inte att ställningstagandet påverkats så mycket av lobbykampanjen från övriga rödgröna partier – däremot skulle sveket mot väljarna vara svårare att hantera än det kommer att innebära att samarbeta med V, även om de står utanför regeringen, säger Madestam och fortsätter: – Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist sa att beslutet var enhälligt i riksdagsgrupp och partistyrelse. Det har säkert varit mycket debatt. Men att hon har sitt parti bakom sig nu, att man har bestämt det här gemensamt är oerhört viktigt. Vi kommer ihåg hur det var för Nyamko Sabuni i Liberalerna när hon svängde, det var inte roligt. Jag tror att den här processen varit viktig för C. S-ledaren Magdalena Andersson och MP-språkrören har sagt att beskedet från C är ”mycket välkommet”. Men nu när C har valt ett vänstersamarbete ökar pressen rejält på både S och V, menar Madestam.

articles.body_text: Planerade du att bunkra månadskort till halverat pris? Ledsen, men endast hos Västtrafik är det möjligt. För resenärer som åker med Västtrafik går det att köpa rabatterade biljetter fram till den 2 december, som man kan aktivera i efterhand. – Vi har de köpvillkor vi har sedan tidigare, att man kan aktivera en biljett inom 30 dagar. Kostnaden för de biljetter som inte täcks av statligt stöd har regionen beslutat om att ta, säger Patrik Chi, presskommunikatör på Västtrafik. Reglerna i andra regioner varierar. Region Skåne har en aktiveringstid på 30 dagar och där går det inte att köpa en rabatterad biljett efter den 2 november. För Länstrafiken Norrbotten är sista dag att köpa en rabatterad biljett den 1 december och sista giltighetstid är 31 december. I Stockholm är den 2 december sista dagen att både aktivera och köpa ett rabatterat kort. – Oavsett om man köper de prissänkta biljetterna på SL-kort eller i appen så aktiveras de automatiskt den 2 december, säger Sophie Gunnarsson, presskommunikatör på Stockholms lokaltrafik SL. Priset på biljetterna sänktes den 1 juli i år och gäller till årsskiftet. Regionerna har fått ersättning från staten för att tillfälligt kunna sänka priserna. Tiotals drönare i riktning mot den ryska huvudstaden Moskva har avvärjts, hävdar stadens borgmästare Sergej Sobjanin. Det ryska luftförsvaret påstås ha skjutit ned ett stort antal attackdrönare, enligt borgmästarens inlägg på Telegram under natten mot måndagen, svensk tid. – Ni kommer att vinna kriget och då kommer ni att ha alla förutsättningar för framgång, sade prinsen till krigsveteraner. Den brittiske prinsen deltog i evenemang i Lviv i västra Ukraina och resan hölls hemlig av säkerhetsskäl. Han träffade bland annat skadade krigsveteraner och vårdpersonal.
